analysis:
Examined both protocol-document excerpts, file metadata, the MLX submodule pointer change, and every supplied GLM policy hunk against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 details. GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift adds nullable reasoning controls, summary no-ops, Boolean/object thinking aliases, replay of returned reasoning, empty history arguments, and acceptance of strict tools. Reserved-schema rejection remains visible; conflicting thinking controls remain rejected. Returned reasoning is applied only to assistant turns lacking reasoningContent and only when message counts align (head 352–362, 394–407). No supplied change directly alters socket authorization, encryption, cache scope, billing usage, or privileged-helper authority. The documentation preserves loaded-model selection and explicitly distinguishes prompt behavior from qualification.
No independently established regression warrants a finding in this scope. Material integration checks remain: returned caller-authored reasoning is inserted after validateHistory (head 351–362), so inspect validateHistory and native template handling to ensure alternate reasoning fields receive the same ambiguous-delimiter protections as reasoning_content (A-001, TB-007, T-007). Removal of strict-tool rejection (head 347–350) relies on ToolConstraintValidation.validate and every output path validating complete calls before exposure; the comment and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md:1152 are not implementation proof. Reconcile these checks with inbound decoding, local HTTP, streaming, and prompt-contract identity/cache bindings (T-041). Finally, libs/mlx-swift-lm:1 changes executable inference dependency code, but only commit pointers were supplied. Review that dependency diff for rendering, tool validation, media, resource bounds and cache behavior under TB-007; its absence prevents a security conclusion about the combined change. Unchanged callers and external platform implementations were not examined.
